what_it_is.prose: Dynamatic Technologies Limited is a Bengaluru-headquartered precision-engineering and aerostructures company, incorporated in 1973 and listed on the BSE (505242) and NSE (DYNAMATECH), led by CEO & Managing Director Udayant Malhoutra. It operates three segments — Aerospace, Hydraulics and Metallurgy — with plants in India, Swindon (UK) and Germany. The Aerospace segment is now the largest, at ₹775.6 crore in FY26 (up 27.6% YoY) and about 48% of total revenue. Dynamatic is a Tier-1/Tier-2 aerostructures supplier: it produces flap-track beam assemblies for the Airbus A320 family and A330 wide-body, delivered the first complete ship-set of Airbus A220 doors ahead of schedule in FY26, and builds parts and aerostructure assemblies for Boeing (CH-47 Chinook, P-8 Poseidon, and F-15EX Eagle II, contracted September 2021), Bell 407 helicopter components, and airframe body parts for HAL's Su-30MKI and Lakshya. For FY26 the company reported total revenue of ₹1,621.3 crore (up 15.5% YoY from ₹1,403.8 crore) and EBITDA of ₹182.7 crore (up 15.4%). Dynamatic's aerospace growth is driven by rising Airbus and Boeing build rates and deeper work-package content, positioning it as one of India's few listed pure-play private aerostructures firms alongside its hydraulics and metallurgy businesses.

deployments_procurement.summary: Dynamatic is a build-to-print and design-and-build aerostructures supplier into global OEM programmes rather than a platform operator; India relevance comes from HAL Su-30MKI/Lakshya work and its role in the Indian private aerospace supply base. Financials are disclosed via BSE/NSE filings.

faq.question: What are Dynamatic Technologies' FY26 financials?
faq.answer: For FY26 Dynamatic reported total revenue of ₹1,621.3 crore, up 15.5% year-on-year from ₹1,403.8 crore, with EBITDA of ₹182.7 crore (up 15.4%). The Aerospace segment grew 27.6% to ₹775.6 crore — about 48% of total revenue — outpacing Hydraulics (₹487.4 cr, +6.4%) and Metallurgy (₹358.1 cr, +6.9%). Q4 FY26 revenue was ₹433.2 crore, up 13.8%.

faq.question: Which aircraft programmes does Dynamatic supply?
faq.answer: Dynamatic builds flap-track beam assemblies for the Airbus A320 family and A330, and delivered the first complete ship-set of Airbus A220 doors ahead of schedule in FY26. For Boeing it makes aerostructures for the CH-47 Chinook, P-8 Poseidon and F-15EX Eagle II (contracted September 2021); it also supplies Bell 407 helicopter components and airframe body parts for HAL's Su-30MKI and Lakshya. Dynamatic is the global single-source supplier of flap-track beam assemblies for both the A320 family and the A330.

faq.question: Is Dynamatic an Indian company and where are its plants?
faq.answer: Yes. Dynamatic Technologies is incorporated in India (1973), headquartered in Bengaluru and listed on the BSE (505242) and NSE (DYNAMATECH), led by CEO & MD Udayant Malhoutra. Besides its Indian facilities it operates aerostructures plants in Swindon (UK) and Germany, making it one of the few listed Indian private pure-play aerostructures suppliers to global OEMs.
